- **Domain docs** — where `CONTEXT.md` and ADRs live, and the consumer rules for reading them

This is a prompt-driven skill, not a deterministic script. Explore, present what you found, confirm with the user, then write.

## Process

### 1. Explore

Look at the current repo to understand its starting state. Read whatever exists; don't assume:

- `git remote -v` and `.git/config` — is this a GitHub repo? Which one?
- `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` at the repo root — does either exist? Is there already an `## Agent skills` section in either?
- `CONTEXT.md` and `CONTEXT-MAP.md` at the repo root
- `docs/adr/` and any `src/*/docs/adr/` directories
- `docs/agents/` — does this skill's prior output already exist?
- `.scratch/` — sign that a local-markdown issue tracker convention is already in use
- Is the `triage` skill installed? (a `triage` skill folder alongside this one, or `triage` in your available skills.) This decides whether Section B runs at all.
- Monorepo signals — a `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, a `workspaces` field in `package.json`, or a populated `packages/*` with its own `src/`. Present only in a genuinely large multi-package repo; their absence means single-context, which is almost every repo.

### 2. Present findings and ask

Summarise what's present and what's missing. Then take the sections in order — one section, one answer, then the next.

Lead each section with the recommended answer so the user can accept it in a word. Give a one-line explainer only when the choice genuinely branches; skip the section entirely when exploration already settled it (Section B when `triage` isn't installed, Section C when there's no monorepo).

**Section A — Issue tracker.**

> Explainer: The "issue tracker" is where issues live for this repo. Skills like `to-tickets`, `triage`, and `to-spec` read from and write to it — they need to know whether to call `gh issue create`, write a markdown file under `.scratch/`, or follow some other workflow you describe. Pick the place you actually track work for this repo.

Default posture: these skills were designed for GitHub. If a `git remote` points at GitHub, propose that. If a `git remote` points at GitLab (`gitlab.com` or a self-hosted host), propose GitLab. Otherwise (or if the user prefers), offer:

- **GitHub** — issues live in the repo's GitHub Issues (uses the `gh` CLI)
- **GitLab** — issues live in the repo's GitLab Issues (uses the [`glab`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli) CLI)
- **Local markdown** — issues live as files under `.scratch/<feature>/` in this repo (good for solo projects or repos without a remote)
- **Other** (Jira, Linear, etc.) — ask the user to describe the workflow in one paragraph; the skill will record it as freeform prose

Record the choice in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`. The GitHub and GitLab templates carry a "PRs as a request surface" flag, defaulted **off** — leave it off and don't raise it; a user who wants external PRs in the triage queue can flip the flag in the file later.

**Section B — Triage label vocabulary.** Skip this section entirely if the `triage` skill isn't installed (exploration told you) — an uninstalled skill needs no labels.

If it is installed, ask exactly one question:

> Do you want to keep the default triage labels? (recommended: **yes**)

The defaults are the five canonical roles, each label string equal to its name: `needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`. On **yes**, write them as-is. Only if the user says no — usually because their tracker already uses other names (e.g. `bug:triage` for `needs-triage`) — collect the overrides so `triage` applies existing labels instead of creating duplicates.

**Section C — Domain docs.** Default to **single-context** — one `CONTEXT.md` + `docs/adr/` at the repo root. This fits almost every repo; write it without asking.

Offer **multi-context** — a root `CONTEXT-MAP.md` pointing to per-context `CONTEXT.md` files — only when exploration found monorepo signals. Then confirm which layout they want.

### 3. Confirm and edit

Show the user a draft of:

- The `## Agent skills` block to add to whichever of `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` is being edited (see step 4 for selection rules)
- The contents of `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`, `docs/agents/domain.md`, and `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` (the last only when `triage` is installed)

Let them edit before writing.

### 4. Write

**Pick the file to edit:**

- If `CLAUDE.md` exists, edit it.
- Else if `AGENTS.md` exists, edit it.
- If neither exists, ask the user which one to create — don't pick for them.

Never create `AGENTS.md` when `CLAUDE.md` already exists (or vice versa) — always edit the one that's already there.

If an `## Agent skills` block already exists in the chosen file, update its contents in-place rather than appending a duplicate. Don't overwrite user edits to the surrounding sections.

The block:

```markdown
## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

[one-line summary of where issues are tracked]. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

### Triage labels

[one-line summary of the label vocabulary]. See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

[one-line summary of layout — "single-context" or "multi-context"]. See `docs/agents/domain.md`.
```

Include the `### Triage labels` sub-block, and write `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`, only when `triage` is installed and Section B ran. When it isn't, both are omitted.

Then write the docs files using the seed templates in this skill folder as a starting point:

- [issue-tracker-github.md](./issue-tracker-github.md) — GitHub issue tracker
- [issue-tracker-gitlab.md](./issue-tracker-gitlab.md) — GitLab issue tracker
- [issue-tracker-local.md](./issue-tracker-local.md) — local-markdown issue tracker
- [triage-labels.md](./triage-labels.md) — label mapping (only if `triage` is installed)
- [domain.md](./domain.md) — domain doc consumer rules + layout

For "other" issue trackers, write `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` from scratch using the user's description.

### 5. Done

Tell the user the setup is complete and which engineering skills will now read from these files. Mention they can edit `docs/agents/*.md` directly later — re-running this skill is only necessary if they want to switch issue trackers or restart from scratch.

1→# Agent-first CLI UX

Grill settled 2026-08-20. ADRs 0001–0005. Seams: spawn CLI + prompt helpers (confirmed).

## Problem Statement

An agent that runs `dora` cannot learn the first loop from `--help`. It dumps a 32-line catalog on a typo. `--capabilities` lists only three verbs. `--json` is rejected. A TTY “proceed?” or “apply?” hangs the agent. The human README already shows `npx skills add` then `dora review --quick`. The binary does not.

## Solution
10→
The binary talks to the Runner. `--help` opens with the same two-line first loop as the README. A new `dora agent-help` is the one live command map (text, `--json`, and per-verb drill-in). Each verb is **read-only** or **writes**. `--capabilities` is removed. `--json` is an alias for `--format json`. A detected agent skips the Scan proceed gate. A detected agent that would write without `--yes` or `--dry-run` gets exit `2` and a Next line — no prompt, no write. Humans on a real TTY still see confirms. Docs change only when a new help line would disagree.

## User Stories

1. As a Runner, I want `dora --help` to start with `npx skills add saif-shines/doraval` then `dora review --quick`, so that I know the first loop without the README.
2. As a Runner, I want `--help` to still list the existing commands after that opener, so that I can discover verbs.
3. As a Reader, I want to still understand `dora --help`, so that a human who opens it is not lost.
4. As a Reader, I want the README Quick start to keep those same two lines, so that GitHub and `--help` do not disagree.
5. As a Runner, I want `dora review --help` to show two or three copy-paste examples, so that I do not guess flags.
20→6. As a Runner, I want `dora review --help` to state exit codes `0` / `1` / `2`, so that I treat the code as truth.
7. As a Runner, I want `dora review --help` to say run `--quick` first, so that Findings show before JSON or Judge.
8. As a Runner, I want `dora fix --help` to show `--dry-run` then `--yes` examples, so that I do not hang on a prompt.
9. As a Runner, I want `dora scan --help` to show bare `dora` and `--yes` / `--json` examples, so that I know Scan is the default.
10. As a Runner, I want `dora nosuch` to print one error and `Next: dora --help`, so that I am not buried in a help dump.
11. As a Runner, I want `dora nosuch` to exit `1`, so that I know the invoke failed.
12. As a Runner, I want `dora nosuch` to print nothing that looks like the full command catalog, so that I go to `--help` next.
13. As a Runner, I want `dora review --json` to emit the same JSON as `--format json`, so that my first guess works.
14. As a Runner, I want `dora review --format json` to keep working, so that existing scripts do not break.
15. As a Runner, I want `--ci` to still imply JSON, so that CI does not change.
30→16. As a Runner, I want JSON data on stdout and errors on stderr, so that pipes stay clean.
17. As a Runner, I want `dora --json` on a Scan to skip the proceed prompt (JSON is already a skip), so that modes stay consistent.
18. As a Runner, I want `dora agent-help` to list every current verb, so that I see the whole map.
19. As a Runner, I want each line labeled **read-only** or **writes**, so that I know what is safe unprompted.
20. As a Runner, I want `dora agent-help --json` to be the same tree as the text map, so that I can branch on fields.
21. As a Runner, I want `dora agent-help review` to show that verb’s flags, examples, exit codes, and label, so that I do not scrape `--help` by hand.
22. As a Runner, I want unknown `dora agent-help nosuch` to say the name is unknown and `Next: dora agent-help`, so that I recover.
23. As a Runner, I want `dora --capabilities` to fail, so that I am not taught a removed flag.
24. As a Runner, I want the shipped skill to name `dora agent-help`, not `--capabilities`, so that the skill matches the binary.
25. As a Runner, I want skill `references/commands.md` to name `agent-help`, so that the short verb list is not stale.
40→26. As a detected agent on a TTY, I want bare `dora` to run Scan with no proceed question, so that I do not hang.
27. As a Reader on a real TTY, I want bare `dora` to still ask proceed, so that I get a beat before the table.
28. As a Runner already on a pipe (non-TTY), I want Scan to stay unprompted, so that today’s contract does not regress.
29. As a Runner passing `--yes`, I want Scan to stay unprompted, so that the old flag still works.
30. As a detected agent, I want `dora fix` without `--yes` or `--dry-run` to exit `2` and print `Next: dora fix . --dry-run`, so that I do not hang and I do not write.
31. As a detected agent, I want `dora reconcile` without `--yes` / `--dry-run` / `--apply` to exit `2` with a Next line, so that I do not write contradictions.
32. As a detected agent, I want `dora memory promote` without `--yes` or `--dry-run` to exit `2` with a Next line, so that I do not write AGENTS.md.
33. As a Reader on a TTY, I want `dora fix` to still confirm each edit, so that a human does not lose the gate.
34. As a Runner passing `--dry-run`, I want to see diffs and write nothing, so that I can preview.
35. As a Runner passing `--yes`, I want mechanical writes to apply, so that I can finish the loop.
50→36. As a Runner, I want `--help` to mention `dora agent-help` after the first loop, so that I find the map.
37. As a Reader, I want `/commands` to keep teaching `--help` and `review --help`, and to mention `agent-help` only if the page would otherwise lie, so that we do not rewrite docs.
38. As a Runner, I want `review`, `scan`, and `fix` to stay **read-only** / **writes** as labeled (review and scan read-only; fix writes), so that the write gate and the map agree.
39. As a Runner, I want `new`, `bump`, `update`, `memory add`, `memory stash`, `memory restore`, and `memory sync` labeled **writes** if they can change disk, so that I do not treat them as safe.
40. As a Runner, I want `sessions`, `providers`, and `agent-help` labeled **read-only**, so that I can run them unprompted.
41. As a Runner, I want `config` and `rules` labeled **writes** when the default invoke can mutate, and **read-only** only if the bare group is help, so that the label is honest.
42. As an implementer, I want one spawn-CLI test seam for all of the above stdout/stderr/exit behavior, so that tests match what agents see.
43. As an implementer, I want the existing confirm helper extended for “is agent?” and “write gate?”, so that TTY prompts are tested without a fake terminal.
44. As a Runner, I want `dora agent-help --json` to include `name`, `label` (`read-only` | `writes`), `description`, `examples`, `exit_codes`, and flags, so that I can parse one object shape.
45. As a Runner, I want JSON errors to stay on stderr, so that `agent-help --json` on success is a clean object.
60→46. As a Reader, I want Scan Intelligence and `dora update` unchanged, so that install health does not move to a new doctor.
47. As a founder, I want no `dora skills get`, no MCP server, no TUI, and no color-default flip in this pass, so that the slice stays shippable.
48. As a Runner, I want `dora review --help` to tell me to look at `dora agent-help review` for the map, not to paste a third flag encyclopedia into the skill.
49. As a CI job, I want `--ci` on review/scan/fix to keep implying JSON and no prompts, so that pipelines do not change.
50. As a Runner using `npx @hacksmith/doraval`, I want the same `--help` opener and `agent-help`, so that PATH vs npx does not fork the story.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Voice.** Top-level `--help` talks to the Runner. Same first loop as README Quick start. Per-command `--help` stays Runner. README / install / get-started stay Reader. ADR 0001.
- **First-loop text (locked).** Exactly two commands, in this order: `npx skills add saif-shines/doraval` then `dora review --quick`. Used on `--help` and already on README.
70→- **`--help` size.** Keep the short citty command list. Do not paste the `agent-help` catalog into `--help`. One line after the opener may point at `dora agent-help`.
- **Per-command help.** `review`, `fix`, and `scan` `--help` each include: what it is, 2–3 examples, exit `0`/`1`/`2`. Review says `--quick` first. Fix shows `--dry-run` then `--yes`.
- **Unknown command.** Exit `1`. One fail line. `Next: dora --help`. No full help reprint. Same for unknown top-level tokens that today dump usage.
- **`--json`.** Alias of `--format json` on every command that already has `--format`. Do not remove `--format json`. `--ci` still implies JSON. Do not move JSON errors onto stdout.
- **`agent-help`.** New visible top-level command. Bare = text table of all current product verbs with label + one example. `--json` = the same tree. `agent-help <name>` = that verb’s page (examples, flags, exit codes, label). Unknown name: exit `1`, `Next: dora agent-help`.
- **Labels.** Only two: `read-only` and `writes`. `scan`, `review`, `sessions`, `providers`, `agent-help` are read-only. `fix`, `reconcile`, `new`, `bump`, `update`, and memory mutators (`add`, `promote`, `stash`, `restore`, `sync`) are writes. `config` and `rules`: bare group (help only) is read-only; mutating subcommands are writes.
- **`--capabilities`.** Remove the flag, the early-exit, and the human banner. Callers get an unknown-flag / unknown-command failure. Reuse the existing manifest builder as the data source for `agent-help` (extend it to every verb + `label`). Do not keep two maps. ADR 0005.
- **Agent detection.** A caller is an agent when stdin/stderr is not a TTY (already), or `CI` is set, or `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, or any name in a small frozen env list (Entire-class: `GEMINI_CLI`, `COPILOT_CLI`, `PI_CODING_AGENT`, plus `CLAUDECODE` if we can verify it in-tree). Tests pin the list. Not a user-facing flag. ADR 0002.
- **Scan interactive gate.** Human TTY + table mode + no `--yes` → still confirm. Detected agent → no confirm, run Scan. JSON/`--ci`/`--yes`/non-TTY unchanged. ADR 0002.
- **Write gate.** For `fix`, `reconcile`, and `memory promote` (and any other confirm-before-write in this slice if cheap): detected agent without `--yes` and without `--dry-run` (and without reconcile `--apply` as the explicit write flag) → no prompt, no write, exit `2`, guided error + `Next:` with the dry-run invoke. Human TTY keeps confirm. ADR 0003.
80→- **Lockstep docs.** Touch README, `/commands`, and the shipped skill / skill references only when a printed line would disagree (first loop, `--capabilities` mentions, `--json`). No homepage rewrite. No new pages. No `dora doctor`.

1→# Issue tracker: GitHub

Issues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.

## Conventions

- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title "..." --body "..."`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.
- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.
- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.
10→- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`
- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label "..."` / `--remove-label "..."`
- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment "..."`

Infer the repo from `git remote -v` — `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.

## Pull requests as a triage surface

**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_

20→When set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:

- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.
- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).
- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.

GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either — resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

30→Create a GitHub issue.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Run `gh issue view <number> --comments`.

## Wayfinding operations

Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.

40→- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.
- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.
- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies** — the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only — the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.
- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.
- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me` — the session's first write.
- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body "<answer>"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.

9→## Core terms
10→
| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **Skill** | A directory with `SKILL.md` (frontmatter + body) that agents load as specialized instructions. |
| **Authored** | Skill origin: a Skill under the current project. |
| **Global** | Skill origin: a Skill under the user home (for example `~/.claude/skills`). |
| **Imported** | Skill origin: a Skill from plugin cache or `node_modules`. Read-only. Not a remove target. |
| **Review** | One `review(path)`. Tiered quality pass over a Skill and/or Memory file: structure → heuristics → optional LLM judge → optional sessions. Workspace and Skill reviews also include cwd Memory files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules`, `copilot-instructions.md`). |
| **Scan** | Fast workspace health check (`dora` bare): agents present, skill validation, shadows/overlaps, install/intelligence. |
| **Rule** | One module (`src/core/rules`). Registry, packages, resolve, stamp, and mutation. CLI only renders and writes config. |
20→| **Package** | Named enable-set of rules: `recommended` (default), `strict`, `minimal`. |
| **Judge** | One module (`judge()`). Owns mode (**api** / **delegate** / **fail**) and transport. Review passes prompt, schema, and `ci`. |
| **Memory** | Product term for principles, artifacts, and always-on files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, …) under `~/.doraval/memory/` and project roots. |
| **Config** | Global product config at `~/.doraval/config.yml`. Code type is still `JournalConfig` (legacy name — not a “journal product”). Holds projects, `eval.*` judge settings, rules, agent command. |
| **Session** | Past agent conversation transcript, normalized via **session adapters** into primitives for evidence and adherence eval. |
| **Finding** | One Skill-check outcome (tier + severity + message + optional rule code / docUrl). The Skill-check module sets `structure` or `heuristics`. Review adds `llm` and `sessions`. Scan presents Skill Findings as health; shadows, overlaps, MCP, budget, and install stay Scan-only. |
| **Review window** | Session evidence span Review already uses: last 10 Sessions, and only Session files newer than 30 days. |
| **Never invoked** | A Skill with no invoke evidence in Sessions inside the Review window. Not the same as a remove candidate. |
| **Recent install** | A Skill added inside the current Review window (`dora new`, `skills add`, copy, or clone). Never invoked is expected. Not a remove candidate. |
| **Remove candidate** | An Authored Skill that is Never invoked and not a Recent install. Its own Finding (new rule). Not R029. Review and Scan may recommend remove. A Global Skill is never a Remove candidate from one project’s Sessions. |
30→| **Quarantine** | Move a Global Skill aside so it can be restored. Not a delete. _Avoid_: stash. |
| **Remove** | Write action (`dora skill remove`). Deletes an Authored Skill. Quarantines a Global Skill. A name is enough. `--for` selects the agent. `--global` selects origin when Authored and Global share a name. One match: just Remove. Several matches (including same agent, two origins): TTY picker; a Runner must pass `--for` / `--global` / a path or it exits `2` with Next. |
| **Restore** | Write action (`dora skill restore`). Puts a Quarantined Global Skill back at its original path (`~/.doraval/quarantine/` plus a record). Does not undo an Authored delete. Git does that. If the original path is occupied, stop. |
| **Explicit remove** | A named Remove. Works on any Authored or Global Skill. Does not require Remove-candidate status. Refuses Imported. |

## Docs voice

Two addressees. Do not mix them on one surface.

1→# Detected agents must pass `--yes` or `--dry-run` to write

`fix`, `reconcile`, and `memory promote` can change the repo. A TTY confirm hangs agents; auto-applying writes is unsafe. A detected agent that runs them bare exits `2` with `Next: … --dry-run`. Humans on a TTY still get the confirm. We rejected “prompt anyway” (hang) and “just write” (silent mutation).

tool_input.new_string:
# Global Skills are never Remove candidates from one project’s Sessions

A Global Skill may be used in other repos. This project’s Sessions cannot prove it is dead. Review and Scan must not recommend remove for Global. `dora skill remove` still Quarantines a Global Skill the user names (Explicit remove). We rejected “recommend from this repo only” (false deletes) and “load every mapped project first” (v1 scope).

# Skill remove

Grill settled 2026-08-21. ADR 0006. Glossary: `CONTEXT.md` (Remove candidate, Never invoked, Recent install, Quarantine, Explicit remove).

Seams (please confirm): **one new Remove planner** (predicate, name resolve, remove/restore plan) + **existing spawn-CLI** (help, write gate, Next, exits). Planner reuses session invoke matching, origin classify, Review window, and the write-gate helpers. No third seam.

## Problem Statement

Skills pile up. A Reader cannot see which ones this project has not invoked in a long time. Review already says **Never invoked**, but it does not recommend remove, and nothing in the CLI removes a Skill. A Runner has no safe write verb. Deleting a Global Skill from one repo’s Sessions would be a false remove. A Skill installed yesterday looks unused and must not be recommended.

## Solution

Review and Scan recommend only a **Remove candidate**: an Authored Skill that is Never invoked in the Review window and is not a Recent install. A new rule (not R029) carries that Finding. Next points at `dora skill remove`.

`dora skill remove` deletes Authored Skills and Quarantines Global Skills. A name is enough. `--for` selects the agent. `--global` selects origin when the name clashes. One match: just Remove. Several matches: TTY picker; a Runner must pass `--for`, `--global`, or a path, or exit `2` with Next.

A Global Skill is never a Remove candidate from this project’s Sessions (ADR 0006). The user can still name it (Explicit remove). That path Quarantines.

`dora skill restore` puts a Quarantined Global Skill back. Authored deletes come back with git. Occupied original path: stop.

Reader and Runner see the same facts. Two voices. Detected agents need `--yes` or `--dry-run` to write.

## User Stories

1. As a Reader, I want Review to tell me which Authored Skills are Remove candidates, so that I know what is safe to drop.
2. As a Reader, I want Scan to show a count of Remove candidates and a Next line, so that bare `dora` leads to cleanup.
3. As a Runner, I want the Remove-candidate Finding to include a Next line to `dora skill remove`, so that I can act without guessing.
4. As a Reader, I want Never invoked and Remove candidate to stay different, so that a yesterday install is not a remove hint.
5. As a Reader, I want a Recent install that was Never invoked to still show R029 only, so that I know it is unused but young.
6. As a Reader, I want a Remove candidate to show the new rule and not also R029, so that one Skill is not two remove-shaped Findings.
7. As a Reader, I want an invoked Authored Skill to show no Remove-candidate Finding, so that live Skills stay quiet.
8. As a Reader, I want a Global Skill that this repo never invoked to stay off the recommend list, so that I do not delete a home Skill used elsewhere.
9. As a Reader, I want to still see that a Global Skill was Never invoked here (R029), so that I have the fact without a remove push.
10. As a Runner, I want Imported Skills refused for Remove, so that I do not break a plugin cache.
11. As a Reader, I want `dora skill remove` to list Remove candidates on a TTY when I pass no name, so that I can pick what to drop.
12. As a Runner, I want bare `dora skill remove` without a name to exit `2` with Next, so that I am not hung on a picker.
13. As a Reader, I want to pass a Skill name and have it Removed when the name is unique, so that the common case is one command.
14. As a Runner, I want `dora skill remove foo --yes` to Remove a unique `foo`, so that I can script it.
15. As a Reader, I want `--for claude` to limit Remove to Claude’s copy, so that I do not touch Grok’s copy.
16. As a Reader, I want a TTY picker when `foo` exists for more than one agent, so that I choose.
17. As a Runner, I want an ambiguous name without `--for` to exit `2` and name the agents, so that I can retry.
18. As a Reader, I want a TTY picker when Claude has both Authored and Global `foo`, so that origin is not guessed.
19. As a Runner, I want `--global` (or a path) when Authored and Global share a name, so that I can disambiguate without a TTY.
20. As a Reader, I want Explicit remove of an invoked Authored Skill I name, so that recommend is not the only door.
21. As a Reader, I want Explicit remove of a Recent install I name, so that I can drop a Skill I just added and do not want.
22. As a Reader, I want Explicit remove of a Global Skill I name, so that there is a way even though it is not a Remove candidate.
23. As a Reader, I want an Authored Remove to delete the Skill directory, so that git can bring it back.
24. As a Reader, I want a Global Remove to Quarantine, not delete, so that I can Restore.
25. As a Reader, I want Quarantine to keep the original path, agent, and time, so that Restore knows where to put it.
26. As a Reader, I want `dora skill restore foo` to put `foo` back at that original path, so that I undo a Global Remove.
27. As a Reader, I want bare `dora skill restore` on a TTY to pick from Quarantine, so that I do not remember names.
28. As a Runner, I want bare `dora skill restore` to exit `2` with Next, so that I pass a name.
29. As a Reader, I want Restore to stop if the original path is occupied, so that I do not overwrite a reinstall.
30. As a Reader, I want Restore to refuse Authored deletes, so that I use git for those.
31. As a Runner, I want `dora skill remove` and `dora skill restore` to be labeled **writes** on `dora agent-help`, so that I do not run them bare.
32. As a Runner, I want a detected agent without `--yes` or `--dry-run` to exit `2` and write nothing, so that I do not hang and I do not mutate.
33. As a Reader on a TTY, I want a confirm before delete or Quarantine, so that I get a beat.
34. As a Runner, I want `--dry-run` to print the plan and write nothing, so that I can preview.
35. As a Runner, I want `--yes` to apply the plan, so that I can finish.
36. As a Runner, I want `--json` to emit the plan or the result, so that I can branch.
37. As a Reader, I want `dora skill --help` to list `remove` and `restore`, so that I find the verbs.
38. As a Runner, I want `dora skill remove --help` to show name, `--for`, `--global`, `--yes`, `--dry-run`, and examples, so that I do not guess.
39. As a Runner, I want `dora agent-help skill` (or `skill remove` / `skill restore`) to describe the write verbs, so that the live map is not stale.
40. As a Reader, I want Scan’s Next for Remove candidates to be `dora skill remove`, so that the hint and the command agree.
41. As a Reader, I want zero Remove candidates to produce no remove Next, so that a clean tree stays quiet.
42. As a Reader, I want a fresh clone (all SKILL.md mtimes young) to treat Authored Skills as Recent installs, so that we miss a recommend rather than push remove after checkout.
43. As a Reader, I want Explicit remove to still work after a fresh clone, so that I can drop a Skill I know I do not want.
44. As a Runner, I want an unknown name to exit `1` with Next `dora skill remove`, so that I recover.
45. As a Runner, I want Imported matches to be listed as refused, so that I know why nothing moved.
46. As a Reader, I want Quarantine to live under the Doraval home (honour `DORAVAL_HOME`), so that tests and machines do not collide.
47. As a Reader, I want Restore of a missing Quarantine name to say nothing is there, so that I am not told it restored.
48. As a CI job, I want `--ci` to imply JSON and no prompts, so that pipelines do not hang.
49. As a Reader, I want `--for` to use the same agent names as `dora new --for`, so that I do not learn a second flag language.
50. As a founder, I want no auto-delete, no Global recommend from one repo, no reuse of memory stash, and no `sdk-dx` API surface, so that v1 stays the grilled shape.
51. As a Runner, I want the new rule to be toggleable like other rules, so that a shop can turn the recommend off.
52. As a Reader, I want the new rule page generated with the catalog, so that the Finding’s docUrl works.
53. As a Reader, I want R029’s wording to stay “Never invoked”, so that we do not say unused.
54. As an implementer, I want one planner module for “is Remove candidate?”, “resolve name”, “plan Remove”, and “plan Restore”, so that CLI and Review/Scan do not fork the rules.
55. As an implementer, I want spawn-CLI tests for help, write gate, Next, and exits, so that Reader and Runner see the same contract as today.
56. As a Reader, I want a path argument to win when I pass one, so that I can point at a specific directory.
57. As a Reader, I want multi-select on the TTY picker, so that I can drop several Remove candidates in one confirm.
58. As a Runner, I want one name per invoke in v1 (or a repeated flag if cheap), so that I do not need a picker.
59. As a Reader, I want `dora --help` to list `skill` if other groups are listed, so that the catalog does not hide the verb.
60. As a Reader, I want README and `/commands` touched only if a printed help line would otherwise lie, so that this is not a docs rewrite.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Glossary.** Use CONTEXT.md terms only. Do not say unused, stale, or stash.
- **ADR 0006.** Global is never a Remove candidate from one project’s Sessions. Explicit remove still Quarantines a named Global Skill.
- **Seams.** One new Remove planner module. Spawn-CLI stays the user-visible seam. Reuse session invoke matching, origin classify (authored / imported / global), Review window constants, write-gate / agent-caller helpers, `nextAction`, `defineGroup`, and the rules registry. Do not add a second planner. Do not reuse the memory-stash folder or APIs.
- **Planner inputs.** Discovered Authored Skills (project skill roots already used by Scan/Review) plus Global Skills under known agent home skill directories. Loaded Sessions for this project only. `now` for Recent install.
- **Never invoked.** Same match as today’s session evidence: native `skillsInvoked`, tool-call path, slash mention. Same Review window: last 10 Sessions, files newer than 30 days.
- **Recent install.** Skill directory (or its SKILL.md) mtime is inside those 30 days. After a fresh clone every Authored Skill may look recent. Accept the miss. Explicit remove still works. Do not read git history in v1.
- **Remove candidate.** Authored AND Never invoked AND not Recent install. Not Global. Not Imported.
- **Findings.** New rule **R034** / slug `remove-candidate`, session family, default warning, on in `recommended`. Bind a new session id. If a Skill is a Remove candidate, emit R034 only (not also R029). If Never invoked but not a Remove candidate (Recent install or Global), emit R029 only. R028 and R030 unchanged.
- **Recommend surface.** Review stamps R034 on that Skill. Scan health lists it and, when the count is > 0, Next: `dora skill remove`. No remove Next when the count is 0.
- **Command group.** `dora skill` with `remove` and `restore`. Bare `dora skill` shows usage. Both are **writes**. Register on the command tree, completions, and `agent-help`.
- **Remove resolve.** Positional name or path. `--for` uses the same agent ids as `dora new --for`. `--global` selects Global origin. Path wins when present. Zero matches: exit `1`, Next `dora skill remove`. Several matches and TTY: picker (multi-select). Several matches and Runner: exit `2`, list matches, Next with `--for` / `--global` / path. One match: proceed to confirm / `--yes` / `--dry-run`.
- **Explicit remove.** A resolved Authored or Global Skill is allowed even when it is not a Remove candidate. Imported: refuse, write nothing for that target.
- **Apply Remove.** Authored: delete the Skill directory. Global: move to `DORAVAL_HOME/quarantine/` plus a record (original path, agent, name, time). Dry-run prints the plan.
- **Restore.** Read Quarantine records. Name or TTY picker. Copy back to original path. If that path exists, write nothing, exit `1`, say it is occupied. No Restore for Authored deletes.
- **Write gate.** Same as ADR 0003: detected agent without `--yes` / `--dry-run` → no prompt, no write, exit `2`, Next with `--dry-run`. Human TTY keeps confirm. `--ci` implies JSON and no prompts.
- **Voice.** `--help` and `agent-help` talk to the Runner. README / get-started stay Reader. Lockstep docs only when a new help line would disagree.
- **Implement skills.** `cli-developer` and `nodejs-cli-best-practices`. Not `sdk-dx` / `sdk-craft`.
- **No version bump** unless the user asks for a release.

## Testing Decisions

- Test external behavior only: predicates, resolve outcomes, plans, filesystem results, stdout/stderr, exit codes. Do not test private helpers.

# Skill remove

Grill settled 2026-08-21. ADR 0006. Glossary: `CONTEXT.md` (Remove candidate, Never invoked, Recent install, Quarantine, Explicit remove).

Seams (please confirm): **one new Remove planner** (predicate, name resolve, remove/restore plan) + **existing spawn-CLI** (help, write gate, Next, exits). Planner reuses session invoke matching, origin classify, Review window, and the write-gate helpers. No third seam.

## Problem Statement

Skills pile up. A Reader cannot see which ones this project has not invoked in a long time. Review already says **Never invoked**, but it does not recommend remove, and nothing in the CLI removes a Skill. A Runner has no safe write verb. Deleting a Global Skill from one repo’s Sessions would be a false remove. A Skill installed yesterday looks unused and must not be recommended.

## Solution

Review and Scan recommend only a **Remove candidate**: an Authored Skill that is Never invoked in the Review window and is not a Recent install. A new rule (not R029) carries that Finding. Next points at `dora skill remove`.

`dora skill remove` deletes Authored Skills and Quarantines Global Skills. A name is enough. `--for` selects the agent. `--global` selects origin when the name clashes. One match: just Remove. Several matches: TTY picker; a Runner must pass `--for`, `--global`, or a path, or exit `2` with Next.

A Global Skill is never a Remove candidate from this project’s Sessions (ADR 0006). The user can still name it (Explicit remove). That path Quarantines.

`dora skill restore` puts a Quarantined Global Skill back. Authored deletes come back with git. Occupied original path: stop.

Reader and Runner see the same facts. Two voices. Detected agents need `--yes` or `--dry-run` to write.

## User Stories

1. As a Reader, I want Review to tell me which Authored Skills are Remove candidates, so that I know what is safe to drop.
2. As a Reader, I want Scan to show a count of Remove candidates and a Next line, so that bare `dora` leads to cleanup.
3. As a Runner, I want the Remove-candidate Finding to include a Next line to `dora skill remove`, so that I can act without guessing.
4. As a Reader, I want Never invoked and Remove candidate to stay different, so that a yesterday install is not a remove hint.
5. As a Reader, I want a Recent install that was Never invoked to still show R029 only, so that I know it is unused but young.
6. As a Reader, I want a Remove candidate to show the new rule and not also R029, so that one Skill is not two remove-shaped Findings.
7. As a Reader, I want an invoked Authored Skill to show no Remove-candidate Finding, so that live Skills stay quiet.
8. As a Reader, I want a Global Skill that this repo never invoked to stay off the recommend list, so that I do not delete a home Skill used elsewhere.
9. As a Reader, I want to still see that a Global Skill was Never invoked here (R029), so that I have the fact without a remove push.
10. As a Runner, I want Imported Skills refused for Remove, so that I do not break a plugin cache.
11. As a Reader, I want `dora skill remove` to list Remove candidates on a TTY when I pass no name, so that I can pick what to drop.
12. As a Runner, I want bare `dora skill remove` without a name to exit `2` with Next, so that I am not hung on a picker.
13. As a Reader, I want to pass a Skill name and have it Removed when the name is unique, so that the common case is one command.
14. As a Runner, I want `dora skill remove foo --yes` to Remove a unique `foo`, so that I can script it.
15. As a Reader, I want `--for claude` to limit Remove to Claude’s copy, so that I do not touch Grok’s copy.
16. As a Reader, I want a TTY picker when `foo` exists for more than one agent, so that I choose.
17. As a Runner, I want an ambiguous name without `--for` to exit `2` and name the agents, so that I can retry.
18. As a Reader, I want a TTY picker when Claude has both Authored and Global `foo`, so that origin is not guessed.
19. As a Runner, I want `--global` (or a path) when Authored and Global share a name, so that I can disambiguate without a TTY.
20. As a Reader, I want Explicit remove of an invoked Authored Skill I name, so that recommend is not the only door.

22. As a Reader, I want Explicit remove of a Global Skill I name, so that there is a way even though it is not a Remove candidate.
23. As a Reader, I want an Authored Remove to delete the Skill directory, so that git can bring it back.
24. As a Reader, I want a Global Remove to Quarantine, not delete, so that I can Restore.
25. As a Reader, I want Quarantine to keep the original path, agent, and time, so that Restore knows where to put it.
26. As a Reader, I want `dora skill restore foo` to put `foo` back at that original path, so that I undo a Global Remove.

29. As a Reader, I want Restore to stop if the original path is occupied, so that I do not overwrite a reinstall.
30. As a Reader, I want Restore to refuse Authored deletes, so that I use git for those.

32. As a Runner, I want a detected agent without `--yes` or `--dry-run` to exit `2` and write nothing, so that I do not hang and I do not mutate.
33. As a Reader on a TTY, I want a confirm before delete or Quarantine, so that I get a beat.
34. As a Runner, I want `--dry-run` to print the plan and write nothing, so that I can preview.
35. As a Runner, I want `--yes` to apply the plan, so that I can finish.
36. As a Runner, I want `--json` to emit the plan or the result, so that I can branch.
37. As a Reader, I want `dora skill --help` to list `remove` and `restore`, so that I find the verbs.
38. As a Runner, I want `dora skill remove --help` to show name, `--for`, `--global`, `--yes`, `--dry-run`, and examples, so that I do not guess.
39. As a Runner, I want `dora agent-help skill` (or `skill remove` / `skill restore`) to describe the write verbs, so that the live map is not stale.
40. As a Reader, I want Scan’s Next for Remove candidates to be `dora skill remove`, so that the hint and the command agree.

43. As a Reader, I want Explicit remove to still work after a fresh clone, so that I can drop a Skill I know I do not want.

49. As a Reader, I want `--for` to use the same agent names as `dora new --for`, so that I do not learn a second flag language.
50. As a founder, I want no auto-delete, no Global recommend from one repo, no reuse of memory stash, and no `sdk-dx` API surface, so that v1 stays the grilled shape.
51. As a Runner, I want the new rule to be toggleable like other rules, so that a shop can turn the recommend off.
52. As a Reader, I want the new rule page generated with the catalog, so that the Finding’s docUrl works.
53. As a Reader, I want R029’s wording to stay “Never invoked”, so that we do not say unused.
54. As an implementer, I want one planner module for “is Remove candidate?”, “resolve name”, “plan Remove”, and “plan Restore”, so that CLI and Review/Scan do not fork the rules.
55. As an implementer, I want spawn-CLI tests for help, write gate, Next, and exits, so that Reader and Runner see the same contract as today.
56. As a Reader, I want a path argument to win when I pass one, so that I can point at a specific directory.
57. As a Reader, I want multi-select on the TTY picker, so that I can drop several Remove candidates in one confirm.
58. As a Runner, I want one name per invoke in v1 (or a repeated flag if cheap), so that I do not need a picker.

# Skill remove

Grill settled 2026-08-21. ADR 0006. Glossary: `CONTEXT.md` (Remove candidate, Never invoked, Recent install, Quarantine, Explicit remove).

Seams (please confirm): **one new Remove planner** (predicate, name resolve, remove/restore plan) + **existing spawn-CLI** (help, write gate, Next, exits). Planner reuses session invoke matching, origin classify, Review window, and the write-gate helpers. No third seam.

## Problem Statement

Skills pile up. A Reader cannot see which ones this project has not invoked in a long time. Review already says **Never invoked**, but it does not recommend remove, and nothing in the CLI removes a Skill. A Runner has no safe write verb. Deleting a Global Skill from one repo’s Sessions would be a false remove. A Skill installed yesterday looks unused and must not be recommended.

## Solution

Review and Scan recommend only a **Remove candidate**: an Authored Skill that is Never invoked in the Review window and is not a Recent install. A new rule (not R029) carries that Finding. Next points at `dora skill remove`.

`dora skill remove` deletes Authored Skills and Quarantines Global Skills. A name is enough. `--for` selects the agent. `--global` selects origin when the name clashes. One match: just Remove. Several matches: TTY picker; a Runner must pass `--for`, `--global`, or a path, or exit `2` with Next.

A Global Skill is never a Remove candidate from this project’s Sessions (ADR 0006). The user can still name it (Explicit remove). That path Quarantines.

`dora skill restore` puts a Quarantined Global Skill back. Authored deletes come back with git. Occupied original path: stop.

Reader and Runner see the same facts. Two voices. Detected agents need `--yes` or `--dry-run` to write.

## User Stories

1. As a Reader, I want Review to tell me which Authored Skills are Remove candidates, so that I know what is safe to drop.
2. As a Reader, I want Scan to show a count of Remove candidates and a Next line, so that bare `dora` leads to cleanup.
3. As a Runner, I want the Remove-candidate Finding to include a Next line to `dora skill remove`, so that I can act without guessing.
4. As a Reader, I want Never invoked and Remove candidate to stay different, so that a yesterday install is not a remove hint.
5. As a Reader, I want a Recent install that was Never invoked to still show R029 only, so that I know it is unused but young.
6. As a Reader, I want a Remove candidate to show the new rule and not also R029, so that one Skill is not two remove-shaped Findings.
7. As a Reader, I want an invoked Authored Skill to show no Remove-candidate Finding, so that live Skills stay quiet.
8. As a Reader, I want a Global Skill that this repo never invoked to stay off the recommend list, so that I do not delete a home Skill used elsewhere.
9. As a Reader, I want to still see that a Global Skill was Never invoked here (R029), so that I have the fact without a remove push.
10. As a Runner, I want Imported Skills refused for Remove, so that I do not break a plugin cache.
11. As a Reader, I want `dora skill remove` to list Remove candidates on a TTY when I pass no name, so that I can pick what to drop.
12. As a Runner, I want bare `dora skill remove` without a name to exit `2` with Next, so that I am not hung on a picker.
13. As a Reader, I want to pass a Skill name and have it Removed when the name is unique, so that the common case is one command.
14. As a Runner, I want `dora skill remove foo --yes` to Remove a unique `foo`, so that I can script it.
15. As a Reader, I want `--for claude` to limit Remove to Claude’s copy, so that I do not touch Grok’s copy.
16. As a Reader, I want a TTY picker when `foo` exists for more than one agent, so that I choose.
17. As a Runner, I want an ambiguous name without `--for` to exit `2` and name the agents, so that I can retry.
18. As a Reader, I want a TTY picker when Claude has both Authored and Global `foo`, so that origin is not guessed.
19. As a Runner, I want `--global` (or a path) when Authored and Global share a name, so that I can disambiguate without a TTY.
20. As a Reader, I want Explicit remove of an invoked Authored Skill I name, so that recommend is not the only door.
21. As a Reader, I want Explicit remove of a Recent install I name, so that I can drop a Skill I just added and do not want.
22. As a Reader, I want Explicit remove of a Global Skill I name, so that there is a way even though it is not a Remove candidate.
23. As a Reader, I want an Authored Remove to delete the Skill directory, so that git can bring it back.
24. As a Reader, I want a Global Remove to Quarantine, not delete, so that I can Restore.
25. As a Reader, I want Quarantine to keep the original path, agent, and time, so that Restore knows where to put it.
26. As a Reader, I want `dora skill restore foo` to put `foo` back at that original path, so that I undo a Global Remove.
27. As a Reader, I want bare `dora skill restore` on a TTY to pick from Quarantine, so that I do not remember names.
28. As a Runner, I want bare `dora skill restore` to exit `2` with Next, so that I pass a name.
29. As a Reader, I want Restore to stop if the original path is occupied, so that I do not overwrite a reinstall.
30. As a Reader, I want Restore to refuse Authored deletes, so that I use git for those.
31. As a Runner, I want `dora skill remove` and `dora skill restore` to be labeled **writes** on `dora agent-help`, so that I do not run them bare.
32. As a Runner, I want a detected agent without `--yes` or `--dry-run` to exit `2` and write nothing, so that I do not hang and I do not mutate.
33. As a Reader on a TTY, I want a confirm before delete or Quarantine, so that I get a beat.
34. As a Runner, I want `--dry-run` to print the plan and write nothing, so that I can preview.
35. As a Runner, I want `--yes` to apply the plan, so that I can finish.
36. As a Runner, I want `--json` to emit the plan or the result, so that I can branch.

# To Tickets

Break a plan, spec, or conversation into a set of **tickets** — tracer-bullet vertical slices, each declaring the tickets that **block** it.

The issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if not.

## Process

### 1. Gather context

Work from whatever is already in the conversation context. If the user passes a reference (a spec path, an issue number or URL) as an argument, fetch it and read its full body and comments.

### 2. Explore the codebase (optional)

If you have not already explored the codebase, do so to understand the current state of the code. Ticket titles and descriptions should use the project's domain glossary vocabulary, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

Look for opportunities to prefactor the code to make the implementation easier. "Make the change easy, then make the easy change."

### 3. Draft vertical slices

Break the work into **tracer bullet** tickets.

<vertical-slice-rules>

- Each slice cuts a narrow but COMPLETE path through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests) — vertical, NOT a horizontal slice of one layer
- A completed slice is demoable or verifiable on its own
- Each slice is sized to fit in a single fresh context window
- Any prefactoring should be done first

</vertical-slice-rules>

Give each ticket its **blocking edges** — the other tickets that must complete before it can start. A ticket with no blockers can start immediately.

**Wide refactors are the exception to vertical slicing.** A **wide refactor** is one mechanical change — rename a column, retype a shared symbol — whose **blast radius** fans across the whole codebase, so a single edit breaks thousands of call sites at once and no vertical slice can land green. Don't force it into a tracer bullet; sequence it as **expand–contract**. First expand: add the new form beside the old so nothing breaks. Then migrate the call sites over in batches sized by blast radius (per package, per directory), each batch its own ticket blocked by the expand, keeping CI green batch to batch because the old form still exists. Finally contract: delete the old form once no caller remains, in a ticket blocked by every migrate batch. When even the batches can't stay green alone, keep the sequence but let them share an integration branch that all block a final integrate-and-verify ticket — green is promised only there.

### 4. Quiz the user

Present the proposed breakdown as a numbered list. For each ticket, show:

- **Title**: short descriptive name
- **Blocked by**: which other tickets (if any) must complete first
- **What it delivers**: the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work

Ask the user:

- Does the granularity feel right? (too coarse / too fine)
- Are the blocking edges correct — does each ticket only depend on tickets that genuinely gate it?
- Should any tickets be merged or split further?

Iterate until the user approves the breakdown.

### 5. Publish the tickets to the configured tracker

Publish the approved tickets. **How** depends on the tracker `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` configured — the tickets are the same either way, only the shape of the blocking edges changes:

- **Local files** → write one file per ticket under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first). Each file's "Blocked by" lists the numbers/titles it depends on. Use the per-ticket file template below — one ticket per file, never a single combined file.
- **A real issue tracker (GitHub, Linear, …)** → publish one issue per ticket in dependency order (blockers first) so each ticket's blocking edges can reference real identifiers. Use the platform's native blocking / sub-issue relationship where it has one; otherwise set each ticket's "Blocked by" to the blocking issues. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label unless instructed otherwise — the tickets are agent-grabbable by construction.

Work the **frontier**: any ticket whose blockers are all done. For a purely linear chain that means top to bottom.

Do NOT close or modify any parent issue.

<local-ticket-template>

# <NN> — <Ticket title>

**What to build:** the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective — not a layer-by-layer implementation list.

**Blocked by:** the numbers/titles of the tickets that gate this one, or "None — can start immediately".

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] Acceptance criterion 1
- [ ] Acceptance criterion 2

</local-ticket-template>

<issue-template>

## Parent

A reference to the parent issue on the tracker (if the source was an existing issue, otherwise omit this section).

## What to build

The end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective — not layer-by-layer implementation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Criterion 1
- [ ] Criterion 2

## Blocked by

- A reference to each blocking ticket, or "None — can start immediately".

</issue-template>

In either form, avoid specific file paths or code snippets — they go stale fast. Exception: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it and note briefly that it came from a prototype. Trim to the decision-rich parts — not a working demo, just the important bits.

1→# Issue tracker: GitHub

Issues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.

## Conventions

- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title "..." --body "..."`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.
- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.
- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.
10→- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`
- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label "..."` / `--remove-label "..."`
- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment "..."`

Infer the repo from `git remote -v` — `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.

## Pull requests as a triage surface

**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_

20→When set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:

- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.
- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).
- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.

GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either — resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

30→Create a GitHub issue.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Run `gh issue view <number> --comments`.

## Wayfinding operations

Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.

40→- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.
- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.
- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies** — the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only — the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.
- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.
- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me` — the session's first write.
- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body "<answer>"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.

FileContent.content:
1→---
name: code-review
description: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes — Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
---

Two-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:

- **Standards** — does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?
- **Spec** — does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?
10→
Both axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.

The issue tracker should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing.

## Process

### 1. Pin the fixed point

Whatever the user said is the fixed point — a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc. If they didn't specify one, ask for it.
20→
Capture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.

Before going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here — not inside two parallel sub-agents.

### 2. Identify the spec source

Look for the originating spec, in this order:

1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.) — fetch via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.
30→2. A path the user passed as an argument.

1→---
name: tdd
description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
---

# Test-Driven Development

TDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle — consult them before and during the loop, not after.

10→When exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

## What a good test is

Tests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification — "user can checkout with valid cart" tells you exactly what capability exists — and survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.

See [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.

## Seams — where tests go

20→A **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.

**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything — agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.

Ask: "What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?"

When the shape of that interface is itself in question — how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose — use the `/codebase-design` skill for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.

## Anti-patterns

30→- **Implementation-coupled** — mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.
- **Tautological** — the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth — a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.
- **Horizontal slicing** — writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead — one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.

## Rules of the loop

- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.
- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.
- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.

name: commit-messages
description: Use when creating git commits, writing commit messages, or when about to run git commit -- enforces structured commit message format with imperative mood, capitalized subjects, 72-char wrapping, and atomic commits

# Writing Commit Messages

## Overview

Every commit message follows a consistent format. The subject line completes the sentence: **"If applied, this commit will _\<your subject line\>_"**. When present, the body explains **why**, not what.

## Detect Project Convention First
20→
Follow existing instructions for commits if present in the repository. Check `git log --oneline -20` to see recent patterns and match the existing style.

**Project convention always wins.** The rules below are the default when no convention is detected.

## References

Consider the following references when creating new commit messages:
- **Subject line rules, body format, URLs, issue references**: [references/COMMIT_FORMAT.md](references/COMMIT_FORMAT.md)
- **Split strategies, anti-rationalizations, and refactoring patterns**: [references/ATOMIC_COMMITS.md](references/ATOMIC_COMMITS.md)
30→- **Complete red flags checklist and mistake patterns**: [references/COMMON_MISTAKES.md](references/COMMON_MISTAKES.md)

## Attribution

**Author:** Andrew Fontaine ([@afontaine](https://gitlab.com/afontaine))

This skill is based on widely-accepted git commit message conventions, with inspiration from:

- [Commit Message Guidelines](https://gist.github.com/robertpainsi/b632364184e70900af4ab688decf6f53) by Robert Painsi
- [OpenStack GitCommitMessages](https://wiki.openstack.org/wiki/GitCommitMessages)
40→- [A Note About Git Commit Messages](http://tbaggery.com/2008/04/19/a-note-about-git-commit-messages.html) by Tim Pope
- [How to Write a Git Commit Message](http://chris.beams.io/posts/git-commit/) by Chris Beams

#38

## What to build

Review and Scan recommend **Remove candidates** only. A Remove candidate is an Authored Skill that is Never invoked in the Review window and is not a Recent install.

A new rule **R034** (`remove-candidate`) carries that Finding. R029 stays “Never invoked.” A Remove candidate emits R034 only. A Recent install or a Global Skill that is Never invoked emits R029 only. Invoked Skills emit neither of those two.

Scan shows a count. When the count is greater than 0, Next is `dora skill remove`. When the count is 0, there is no remove Next.

No write in this ticket. `dora skill remove` does not have to exist yet.

- [ ] Invoked Authored Skill → no R034
- [ ] Scan lists Remove candidates and prints Next `dora skill remove` only when count > 0
- [ ] Do not say “unused” or “stash”

None — can start immediately.

1→# Contributing to doraval

## Setup

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run dev -- --help    # run the CLI from source
```

10→Requires Bun ≥ 1.3.0 (see `engines` in `package.json`).

## Before you send a PR

```bash
bun test           # 615+ tests must pass
bun run typecheck  # baseline has pre-existing errors; don't add new ones
```

CI (`.github/workflows/test.yml`) runs `bun test` on Linux, macOS, and Windows. The matrix must be green.
20→
## Code philosophy

Read `AGENTS.md` first. It has the ponytail ladder (YAGNI → reuse → stdlib → installed deps → shortest form → minimum code) this codebase is written against. In short:

- Deletion and reuse beat new surface. Don't add an abstraction for one caller.
- Non-trivial logic gets one small test, not a suite.
- Never skip trust-boundary validation, data-loss error paths, or security handling.

## Commits
30→
Conventional Commits style (`fix:`, `feat:`, `docs:`, `chore:`), matching `git log` and `CHANGELOG.md`. Keep the subject under ~70 chars; explain *why* in the body when it isn't obvious from the diff.

## Version bumps

Don't bump the version in a PR. Releases are cut by maintainers via `bun run bump` / `bun run release` (see `WIP.md` for current release status and policy).

## Filing issues

Prefer `dora report` from inside a project using doraval. It drafts a sanitized issue (no env values, no secrets) with the diagnostic payload maintainers need. Manual issues are fine too.

1→# Commit Format Reference

Complete guide to commit message formatting, line wrapping, and conventions.

## Contents
- Subject line rules
- Body format and wrapping
- Long URLs
- Issue references
10→- Conventional Commits compatibility

## Subject Line Rules

| Rule | Example | Violation | Why |
|------|---------|-----------|-----|
| Capitalize first word | `Add CPU arch filter` | `add CPU arch filter` | Sentence case always |
| Imperative mood | `Fix null pointer` | `Fixed null pointer` | Command form: Add/Fix/Remove |
| 72 char max | `Add CPU arch filter support` | `Add CPU architecture filter to scheduler...` | Hard limit |
| No trailing period | `Add user auth` | `Add user auth.` | Subject is title, not sentence |
20→| No scope prefix | `Fix null pointer in auth` | `auth: fix null pointer` | Unless Conventional Commits |
| Meaningful standalone | `Add CPU arch filter support` | `Fix #847` | Readable outside platform |

```bash
# ✅ Correct
Add CPU arch filter scheduler support

# ❌ Wrong
added cpu arch filter scheduler support    # lowercase, past tense
```
30→
## Body Format and Wrapping

### Blank line after subject (critical)

```bash
# ✅ Correct
Add CPU arch filter support

In a mixed environment of x86 and ARM nodes, the scheduler
40→could not distinguish architectures.

# ❌ Wrong (no blank line)
Add CPU arch filter support
In a mixed environment of x86 and ARM nodes...
```

### Wrap at 72 characters

Exception: URLs and code that can't be split.
50→
### Explain WHY, not WHAT

The diff shows what changed; the message explains why:

```bash
# ✅ Correct
Add CPU arch filter support

In a mixed environment of x86 and ARM nodes, the scheduler
60→could not distinguish architectures, causing crashes.

# ❌ Wrong (only describes WHAT)
Add CPU arch filter support

Added arch label to nodes and filter to algorithm.
```

### Describe effects and limitations

70→```bash
Add CPU arch filter support

Enables workloads to be scheduled only on compatible
architectures. Current limitation: only x86 and ARM
supported. New architectures require updating enum.
```

## Long URLs

80→Put URLs on their own line or use reference-style:

```bash
# Option 1: URL on own line
Implement the technique described at:

https://example.com/very/long/url/exceeds/72/chars

# Option 2: Reference-style
Implement the technique at [1] to prevent exhaustion.
90→
[1] https://example.com/very/long/url/exceeds/72/chars
```

## Issue References

**Only add if project uses them** (check `git log --oneline -20`).

Put in **body** on **own line** at end:

100→```bash
# ✅ Correct
Add CPU arch filter support

[explanation]

Fixes #847

# ❌ Wrong (in subject)
Fix #847: Add CPU arch filter
110→```

**Keywords:** `Fixes #N`, `Closes #N`, `Resolves #N` (GitHub/GitLab), `PROJ-123` (Jira)

## Full Example

```
Add CPU arch filter scheduler support

In a mixed environment of x86 and ARM nodes, the scheduler
120→previously could not distinguish between architectures,
leading to binary incompatibility crashes.

Add an arch label to each node and a corresponding filter
in the scheduling algorithm. This enables workloads to be
scheduled only on compatible architectures.

Current limitation: only x86 and ARM are supported. Adding
new architectures requires updating the label enum.

130→Fixes #847
```

## Conventional Commits Compatibility

If project uses Conventional Commits, use this format:

```bash
<type>(<scope>): <subject>

140→feat(scheduler): add CPU arch filter support
fix(auth): handle null session token
chore(deps): update lodash to 4.17.21
```

**Common types:**
- `feat:` - new feature
- `fix:` - bug fix
- `chore:` - maintenance
- `docs:` - documentation
150→- `refactor:` - code change (no fix/feature)
- `test:` - tests
- `perf:` - performance

All other rules still apply (imperative, 72-char limit includes prefix, body explains WHY).

## Gotchas

- **72-char limit includes type prefix** — `feat(scheduler): ` counts toward 72
- **Blank line is critical** — many tools parse on this boundary
160→- **Issue refs in body, not subject** — keeps subject meaningful
- **URLs break wrapping rule** — put on own line
- **Capitalize after colon** — `feat: Add auth` not `feat: add auth` (unless project uses lowercase)

1→## Parent

#38

## What to build

`dora skill remove <name>` deletes one unique Authored Skill.

A name is enough when only one Authored or resolvable match exists. Explicit remove works even if the Skill is not a Remove candidate. Imported Skills are refused. Nothing is written without `--yes` or `--dry-run` for a detected agent. A human on a TTY still confirms.
10→
`--dry-run` prints the plan and writes nothing. `--yes` deletes the Authored directory. `--json` emits the plan or the result. `--help` and `agent-help` list `skill` / `skill remove` as **writes**. `--for` uses the same agent names as `dora new --for`.

Name clashes, Global Quarantine, Restore, and the bare TTY candidate picker are later tickets. If the name is not unique, fail with a clear Next (do not guess).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `dora skill` and `dora skill remove` exist; bare `dora skill` shows usage
- [ ] Unique Authored name → delete the Skill directory (`--yes`)
- [ ] `--dry-run` writes nothing
20→- [ ] Detected agent without `--yes` / `--dry-run` → exit `2`, no write, Next includes `--dry-run`
- [ ] Human TTY still confirms
- [ ] Explicit remove of a non-candidate Authored Skill works
- [ ] Imported match is refused; that target is not written
- [ ] Unknown name → exit `1`, Next `dora skill remove`
- [ ] Ambiguous name → do not delete; tell the user to disambiguate (full clash UX is the next ticket)
- [ ] `dora skill remove --help` and `agent-help` describe the write verb
- [ ] `--json` / `--ci` work; `--ci` does not prompt
